The present application relates to a method for diagnosing a disease in a subject, comprising determining the presence or absence of one or more circular RNAs (circRNAs) in a bodily fluid sample obtained from said subject, wherein the presence or absence of said one or more circRNAs is indicative of the disease.

In particular, the application relates to a method for diagnosing a neurodegenerative disease, preferably Alzheimer’s disease, in a subject, comprising the steps of:

— determining the level of one or more circRNAs in a bodily fluid sample obtained from said subject; and  
— comparing the determined level with a control level of said one or more circRNAs;

wherein a difference between the determined level and the control level is indicative of the disease.

Furthermore, the application relates to means for detecting circRNAs that serve as biomarkers for a neurodegenerative disease, as well as to kits and arrays comprising nucleic acid probes for detecting exon-exon junctions in a head-to-tail arrangement of these circRNAs.

The application concerns a diagnostic approach for identifying a disease in a subject, which includes assessing whether one or more circular RNAs (circRNAs) are present or absent in a bodily fluid sample obtained from that subject. The detection or non-detection of the one or more circRNAs serves as an indication of the disease.

More specifically, the application is directed to a method for diagnosing a neurodegenerative disorder, preferably Alzheimer’s disease, in a subject. The method involves measuring the amount of one or more circRNAs in a bodily fluid sample from the subject and comparing the measured amount with a reference or control level for the same one or more circRNAs. A difference between the measured level and the control level indicates the presence of the disease.

The application also covers tools for identifying circRNAs that function as biomarkers for neurodegenerative disease, as well as kits and arrays containing nucleic acid probes designed to detect exon-exon junctions arranged in a head-to-tail configuration within these circRNAs.

The application describes a diagnostic method based on determining whether one or more circular RNAs are present or absent in a bodily fluid sample obtained from a subject. In this method, the detection of specific circular RNAs, or the failure to detect them, is used as an indicator of the presence, absence, or likelihood of a disease.

The method is particularly directed to the diagnosis of neurodegenerative diseases. In preferred embodiments, the disease to be diagnosed is Alzheimer’s disease. The diagnostic approach may involve measuring the level of one or more selected circular RNAs in the subject’s sample and comparing that measured level with a control level, such as a level observed in healthy individuals or in subjects not affected by the disease. A difference between the measured level and the control level may be used to support a diagnosis or to indicate an increased risk of disease.

The application further relates to tools and products for carrying out this diagnostic method. These include detection tools, diagnostic kits, and arrays comprising nucleic acid probes. The probes are designed to identify circular RNA-specific exon-exon junctions, particularly junctions formed in a head-to-tail arrangement, which are characteristic of circular RNA molecules. Such tools may therefore be used to detect the relevant circular RNAs in bodily fluid samples and assist in disease diagnosis.
outputs.L4:
The present text relates to methods and materials for diagnosing diseases, in particular Alzheimer’s disease and other neurodegenerative disorders, by detecting circular RNAs in biological samples obtained from a subject. Circular RNAs, or circRNAs, are RNA molecules formed by back-splicing events that create covalently closed RNA circles. Unlike linear RNAs, circRNAs contain a characteristic head-to-tail exon junction, which provides a unique sequence feature that can be specifically detected. Because circRNAs can be stable in bodily fluids and may show disease-associated changes in abundance, they can serve as useful biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, and disease monitoring.

In one embodiment, a bodily fluid sample is obtained from a subject suspected of having a disease or being at risk of developing a disease. The sample may include, for example, blood, plasma, serum, cerebrospinal fluid, saliva, urine, or another biological fluid. RNA is isolated from the sample, or the sample is otherwise processed to permit detection of one or more circRNAs. The presence, absence, or amount of selected circRNAs is then measured using a detection method capable of distinguishing circular RNA molecules from corresponding linear transcripts.

The diagnostic method involves comparing the level of one or more circRNAs in the subject’s sample with a control level. The control may be obtained from healthy individuals, from subjects without the relevant disease, from an established reference range, or from a prior sample taken from the same subject. If the circRNA level in the test sample differs from the control level, the difference may indicate the presence of disease, increased risk of disease, disease progression, or response to treatment. Such differences may include increased expression, decreased expression, complete absence, or altered relative abundance of one or more circRNAs.

The method is particularly applicable to Alzheimer’s disease, but it may also be used in connection with other neurodegenerative diseases, including Parkinson’s disease, Huntington’s disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, frontotemporal dementia, vascular dementia, and related neurological conditions. Different diseases may be associated with distinct circRNA expression patterns or signatures. Accordingly, a panel of circRNAs may be measured to improve diagnostic accuracy, distinguish among different neurological disorders, or classify disease stage.

Detection of circRNAs may be performed using probes, primers, or other binding molecules designed to recognize the head-to-tail junction that is unique to the circular form of the RNA. For example, a probe may span the junction sequence so that it hybridizes only to the circular RNA and not to the corresponding linear messenger RNA. Suitable detection techniques may include reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, quantitative PCR, digital PCR, sequencing, microarray analysis, hybridization assays, or other nucleic acid detection platforms.

The text also contemplates diagnostic kits and arrays for carrying out the method. A kit may include one or more probes or primer sets specific for circRNA junction sequences, reagents for RNA extraction or amplification, control materials, and instructions for comparing detected circRNA levels with reference values. An array may include a plurality of probes fixed to a solid support, each probe being designed to detect a specific circRNA by binding to its head-to-tail exon junction. Such arrays may allow simultaneous detection of multiple circRNAs in a single sample, thereby generating a disease-associated circRNA profile.

In use, the circRNA profile from a patient sample is analyzed and compared with a control profile. A statistically significant difference between the patient profile and the control profile may be interpreted as indicative of a disease state or risk condition. In some embodiments, the method may be used alone as a diagnostic test. In other embodiments, it may be combined with clinical evaluation, imaging data, cognitive testing, genetic testing, protein biomarkers, or other molecular assays to support a more comprehensive diagnosis.

Thus, the described technology provides a biomarker-based approach for detecting neurodegenerative disease through measurement of circular RNAs in bodily fluids. By targeting circRNA-specific junctions, the method enables selective identification of circular RNA molecules and supports the development of diagnostic kits, probe arrays, and related assay systems for disease detection and monitoring.
outputs.L5:
**The Role of RNA in Alzheimer’s Disease**

Alzheimer’s disease is a progressive brain disorder that affects memory, thinking, and behavior. While much research has focused on proteins such as amyloid-beta and tau, scientists are increasingly studying the role of RNA in the development and progression of Alzheimer’s.

RNA is a molecule that helps carry genetic instructions from DNA and supports the production of proteins in cells. In the brain, RNA is essential for normal communication between neurons, cell repair, and maintaining healthy brain function. When RNA processes become disrupted, brain cells may struggle to function properly, which can contribute to neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer’s.

Researchers have found that certain types of RNA, including messenger RNA, microRNA, and long non-coding RNA, may influence inflammation, protein buildup, and cell death in the brain. These RNA changes could help explain why some neurons become damaged over time in Alzheimer’s disease. Because of this, RNA is being explored as both a biomarker for early diagnosis and a possible target for future treatments.

The study of RNA offers new hope for understanding Alzheimer’s more deeply. By learning how RNA affects brain health, scientists may be able to develop better tools for detecting the disease earlier and creating therapies that slow or prevent its progression.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise patent application summary describing methods, kits, and arrays for detecting circRNA biomarkers of neurodegenerative disease.
counterfactuals.output:
## Patent Application Summary

Disclosed are methods, kits, and arrays for detecting circular RNA (circRNA) biomarkers associated with neurodegenerative disease. In certain embodiments, the methods comprise obtaining a biological sample from a subject, isolating or enriching RNA, and detecting the presence, absence, or expression level of one or more circRNAs whose abundance is correlated with a neurodegenerative disease state, disease risk, subtype, progression, prognosis, or therapeutic response.

The neurodegenerative disease may include, without limitation, Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, frontotemporal dementia, Huntington’s disease, Lewy body dementia, or mild cognitive impairment. Suitable biological samples include blood, plasma, serum, cerebrospinal fluid, saliva, urine, extracellular vesicles, neural tissue, or other sample types containing circRNA.

In some embodiments, circRNAs are detected using probes, primers, capture agents, or sequencing methods configured to identify back-splice junctions characteristic of circRNAs. Detection may be performed by quantitative PCR, digital PCR, reverse-transcription PCR, RNA sequencing, microarray hybridization, in situ hybridization, nanostring-based assays, CRISPR-based detection, or other nucleic acid detection platforms. Expression levels of one or more circRNA biomarkers may be compared with a reference value, control sample, or disease classifier to generate a diagnostic, prognostic, or monitoring output.

Also disclosed are kits comprising reagents for detecting one or more neurodegenerative disease-associated circRNAs, including junction-specific primers or probes, reverse transcription reagents, amplification reagents, buffers, controls, standards, and instructions for use. In certain embodiments, the kit further includes reagents for RNA enrichment, RNase R treatment, extracellular vesicle isolation, sample stabilization, or normalization to one or more reference RNAs.

Further disclosed are arrays comprising a solid support bearing a plurality of immobilized probes specific for circRNA back-splice junctions associated with neurodegenerative disease. The arrays may be configured for multiplex detection of circRNA panels, optionally together with linear RNA, microRNA, protein, or metabolite markers. The detected circRNA profile may be used alone or in combination with clinical, genetic, imaging, or cognitive data to classify a subject, monitor disease progression, select or adjust therapy, or identify subjects for clinical trials.

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose an invention disclosure abstract about using exon-exon junction probes to detect head-to-tail circRNAs as biomarkers for diagnosing neurodegenerative diseases.
counterfactuals.output:
**Invention Disclosure Abstract**

Disclosed herein are compositions and methods for detecting circular RNAs (circRNAs) as biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases using exon-exon junction probes specific for head-to-tail back-splice junctions. The invention exploits the unique covalently closed structure of circRNAs, in which a downstream splice donor is joined to an upstream splice acceptor, creating a junction not present in corresponding linear RNA transcripts. In certain embodiments, oligonucleotide probes, primers, capture probes, or reporter probes are designed to hybridize across these circRNA-specific exon-exon junctions, thereby selectively detecting target circRNAs while minimizing detection of linear mRNA isoforms.

The disclosed methods may be applied to biological samples including blood, plasma, serum, cerebrospinal fluid, saliva, extracellular vesicles, neural tissue, or cell-derived RNA. Detection may be performed using quantitative PCR, digital PCR, microarrays, next-generation sequencing enrichment, fluorescence in situ hybridization, electrochemical biosensors, or other nucleic acid detection platforms. In some embodiments, the assays include RNase R treatment or other linear RNA depletion steps to enhance circRNA specificity, although junction-spanning probe design may permit detection without such enrichment.

The circRNAs detected by the disclosed probes may serve as diagnostic, prognostic, stratification, or treatment-monitoring biomarkers for neurodegenerative conditions, including Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Huntington’s disease, frontotemporal dementia, multiple sclerosis-associated neurodegeneration, and related disorders. A panel of circRNA junction probes may be used to generate a disease-associated expression signature that distinguishes affected subjects from healthy controls or differentiates among neurodegenerative disease subtypes.

The invention further provides kits comprising one or more head-to-tail circRNA junction probes, assay reagents, controls, and instructions for detecting circRNA biomarkers in patient samples. The disclosed technology enables sensitive, specific, and minimally invasive assessment of circRNA biomarkers associated with neurodegenerative disease onset, progression, and therapeutic response.
